Definition: properly, a standing, i.e. a spot; but used widely of a locality (general or specific); also (figuratively) of a condition (of body or mind)
BiblicalUsage: mâqôwm is a place, a standing spot, and it is one of the commonest words in the Bible. In Genesis 31:55 Laban returns to his place, and in Exodus 3:5 the place where Moses stands is holy ground. In Deuteronomy 12:5 the place God chooses to put His name is the place of worship, and in Genesis 28:17 Jacob calls Bethel the house of God and the gate of heaven. A place in Scripture is never only ground.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mâqôwm teaches me that God hallows places. I hold that the ground where He meets me becomes holy, whether it is a bush, a dream, or a chosen mountain.
